notes:
I don't have any notes on Proverbs 13 for you yet. I tried to read the source pages, but the tool cut me off before I could see what came back.

**What happened:** I asked for six chapter pages at once: Enduring Word, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and Ellicott on biblehub.com, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes. Something came back, but it wasn't in the format my code expected, so it crashed. My next attempt to look at the results was blocked because I had reached my limit of tool calls for this turn. I never read any of the text, and my other tools can't reach the internet.

**Why the notes are empty:** Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I couldn't read anything, writing "v. 1: …" notes now would mean making them up or attaching URLs I haven't checked.

**What I'll do when you reply "continue":**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, and Matthew Henry, Benson and Barnes where they are available on biblehub.com or studylight.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** The likeliest verses are v. 24 (the rod and physical discipline), vv. 21–22 and 25 (prosperity for the righteous) and v. 12 (hope deferred). I'll check sources such as Wesley's Notes, Gill, desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, gotquestions.org and the Lutheran sites, and report only real differences I find.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes (especially the hard Hebrew in vv. 8, 15 and 23), bibleodyssey.org, Catholic and Orthodox sites, and whatever the sites say about prosperity-teaching readings of vv. 4, 21–22 and 25.

To make it manageable, I'll fetch fewer pages per call and write the notes from what I actually read, each with its URL.
